title: Elements of nonnegative valuation lie in the DVR
statement: Let B be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field K and normalized valuation v:K^\times\to\mathbf Z. If x\in K^\times satisfies v(x)\ge0, then x\in B.

source.place: Algebra Definition 00IE (algebra-definition-value-group): a DVR is the valuation ring of its valuation, B = \{0\}\cup\{x\in K^\times : v(x)\ge0\}

mathlib_searches.results: IsDiscreteValuationRing.lean:67 theorem exists_lift_of_le_one {x : K} (H : ((maximalIdeal A).valuation K) x ≤ (1 : ℤᵐ⁰)) : ∃ a : A, algebraMap A K a = x, for A a DVR and IsFractionRing A K; maximalIdeal A (line 41) is the maximal ideal as a height-one prime, whose adic valuation is the normalized one (uniformizer ↦ ofAdd (-1))

mathlib_match.how: exact match in multiplicative notation: for a DVR A with fraction field K, the normalized valuation of the maximal ideal is (maximalIdeal A).valuation K : K → ℤᵐ⁰ with v_mult = exp(-v), so v(x) ≥ 0 iff v_mult(x) ≤ 1, and the conclusion ∃ a : A, algebraMap A K a = x is x ∈ B
